title: Choose the next rehearsal, not a permanent winner
audience: A fictional workshop coordinator comparing handout workflows
question: Which workflow meets the supplied quality gate for the next rehearsal?
summary: Tray meets the gate with 1 mislabelled set out of 40; Stack is 6 minutes faster but has 4 and exceeds the cap of 2.
context: Explicitly fictional classroom planning data: one scripted run per workflow, not a real benchmark.

sources.title: Fictional handout assembly rehearsal notes
sources.note: The decision rule is supplied by this exercise, not inferred from the chart.

claims.text: Tray takes 24 minutes and Stack takes 18 minutes for 40 sets each.
Tray has 1 mislabelled set and Stack has 4; the eligibility cap is 2 per 40 sets.
Only Tray meets the supplied gate in these rehearsals, despite taking 6 more minutes.
claims.basis: 1 is at most 2, 4 exceeds 2, and 24 minus 18 is 6.
claims.uncertainty: Single scripted runs do not establish repeat-run reliability.

claims.text: Use Tray for the next rehearsal; repeat both workflows before adopting a standing process.
claims.scope: Planning proposal only. No purchase or deployment is authorized.

beats.title: Stack is faster in the supplied run
beats.text: Hold output quantity constant: each workflow assembles 40 sets.
beats.narration: These fictional rehearsals each assemble forty sets. Tray takes twenty-four minutes; Stack takes eighteen. Stack is six minutes faster in these runs. Time alone is not the decision rule.

visual.title: Preparation time for 40 sets
visual.description: One fictional rehearsal per workflow. The shorter bar is faster, not necessarily eligible.
visual.caption: Source: workshop-notes, workflows. No run-to-run interval was supplied.

beats.title: Apply the quality gate first
beats.text: The supplied cap is 2 mislabelled sets per 40.
beats.narration: The cap is two mislabelled sets per forty. Tray has one; Stack has four. Only Tray meets this gate. That is a comparison against a supplied criterion, not proof of a reliable long-term winner.

visual.title: Mislabelled sets; cap is 2
visual.description: Counts out of 40 sets per workflow. The supplied eligibility cap is 2.
visual.caption: Source: workshop-notes, workflows and decision_rule. Lower is preferable under this rule.

question.prompt: Does being 6 minutes faster make Stack eligible?
question.answer: No. Its 4 mislabelled sets exceed the cap of 2, even though it takes 18 rather than 24 minutes.

beats.title: Make a bounded proposal
beats.text: Propose Tray next. Repeat both before standardizing.
beats.narration: The proposal is to use Tray for the next rehearsal, then repeat both workflows before standardizing. The notes contain no repeat-run distribution and do not authorize a purchase or deployment.

limitations: The data and decision rule are fictional.
One scripted run per workflow supplies no repeat-run uncertainty estimate.
The proposal does not establish general superiority or authorize an external action.
